title: [NEXT-704] `next-env.d.ts` not created automatically when running `next lint`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: Linting
labels.description: Related to `next lint` or ESLint with Next.js.

labels.name: linear: next
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Next.js team.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

    Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.3.0: Mon Jan 30 20:38:37 PST 2023; root:xnu-8792.81.3~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
    Binaries:
      Node: 18.12.1
      npm: 9.2.0
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: 7.27.1
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.1.7-canary.20
      eslint-config-next: 13.1.7-canary.20
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0

### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

ESLint (eslint-config-next)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/distracted-darkness-t8296y

### To Reproduce

1.  Create a new app using `reproduction-app` example:

    ```sh
    npx create-next-app@latest --example reproduction-app reproduction-app
    cd reproduction-app
    ```

1.  Autoconfigure ESLint:

    ```sh
    yarn next lint
    ```
    
    This will install missing dependencies and also create `.eslintrc.json` file.


1.  Check if `next-env.d.ts` is automatically re-created on `dev`:

    ```sh
    rm next-env.d.ts
    yarn dev
    ## ctrl+c
    ls next-env.d.ts ## ✅
    ```
    
    > Note that Sandbox UI does not show ignored files
    
1.  Check if `next-env.d.ts` is automatically re-created on `build`:

    ```sh
    rm next-env.d.ts
    yarn build
    ls next-env.d.ts ## ✅
    ```

1.  Check if `next-env.d.ts` is automatically re-created on `lint`:

    ```sh
    rm next-env.d.ts
    yarn next lint
    ls next-env.d.ts ## ❌ ls: cannot access 'next-env.d.ts': No such file or directory
    ```

### Describe the Bug

[Docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/typescript) recommend to keep `next-env.d.ts` in `.gitignore`, which makes sense. The file is generated by Next.js automatically on `next dev` and `next build`.

I configured a new project as recommended and noticed that my local output of ESLint was different to what I saw in CI. After some investigation, it turned out that running `yarn install; yarn next lint` in GitHub Workflows was not creating `next-env.d.ts`, so some `@typescript-eslint/*` rules were behaving differently.

Running `git add next-env.d.ts --force; git commit; git push` helped as a temp workaround. My older projects do not contain `next-env.d.ts` in `.gitignore`, so the problem is not vivid there.

### Expected Behavior

Since `next dev` and `next build` autogenerate `next-env.d.ts` if missing, I would expect the same to happen when running `next lint`. This can be useful primarily in CI and will save other developers from a trap I have fallen into.

I also wonder if there is room for something like `next warmup` / `next codegen`, which could be executed separately. Use case: `yarn install; yarn warmup; yarn tsc --noEmit`.
